newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mixed.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids were mixed on Friday as merchandisers in Minnesota, the Dakotas and Montana reported scant farm sales.
A raft of weather-related problems plagued merchandisers and farmers in Minneapolis and North Dakota.
Grain terminals are preparing for high water on rivers near Minneapolis by making plans for sandbagging operations and evacuating facilities, grain officials said.

The St Paul District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers expects the Minnesota River level to reach 23 feet within 24 hours in western Minnesota, nine feet above flood stage. Rainfall has been forecast for most of Minnesota and western Wisconsin for this weekend, the Corps said late Friday.
"The rapid (snow) melt and forecast rainfall will result in much higher crests on the Minnesota, Mississippi, and St Croix Rivers," the Corps said.
At Savage, Minn., the Minnesota was forecast to rise 1.2 feet in the next 24 hours. However, the Corps said the river should crest below the record set in 1993.

Some flooding in parts of North Dakota also hampered movement. Runoff from the melting winter snowpack pooled into vast lakes across the northern plains, pushing floodwaters into rural towns, authorities said. Several tributaries of the north-flowing Red River had already reached record crests, and overland flooding blocked highways and swamped several small North Dakota towns.
